title: Substitutions (Textable, Record)
documentation:
## Purpose

Substitutions carry a JSON object whose keys and values are plain strings. They are used to fill template placeholders in queries, prompts, or other parameterized content before execution.

## When to use

Use this media type when a node needs to receive a dynamic set of variable bindings at runtime. Pair it with [Query Name](https://capdag.com/browse/media:query-name;textable) to identify the query to execute and supply the values that replace its placeholders.

## Notes

Keys and values must both be strings. Nesting is not supported; flatten complex structures into dot-separated or underscore-separated key names before passing them as substitutions.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
